previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and chronic graft-versus-host disease presented with worsening lower extremity ulcers, increased pain, and malodorous discharge. He had recently undergone dental work without antibiotic prophylaxis. Admission labs showed leukocytosis and mild renal impairment. A wound swab grew sparse Pseudomonas aeruginosa, sensitive to multiple antibiotics. Given his immunocompromised state and increased pain, he was treated with a seven-day course of IV piperacillin-tazobactam. Dermatology recommended enhanced wound care with Dakin’s solution and alternating topical metronidazole and gentamicin. Diarrhea developed during treatment, attributed to antibiotics; it resolved with loperamide and hydration. His infection markers improved, pain decreased, and wounds showed clinical improvement. He was discharged home with oral azithromycin, continued topical therapies, and close follow-up with wound care and research teams.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ year old male with PMHx of AML s/p MUD 
allogenic BMT (___), complicated by relapse (___), and 
extensive chronic GVHD, most notably of bilateral lower 
extremities. Patient has had MSSA pneumonia, bacteremia ___ leg 
wounds, sclerodermatous skin breakdown, and recurrent 
pseudomonas, ___ addition to a mild restrictive ventilatory 
defect. He presented to ___ with ___ weeks of worsening BLE 
pain, discharge, and erythema, concerning for infection (pt w/ 
hx of Pseudomonal skin/soft tissue infection ___ past, 
necessitating admissions to hospital) for which patient was 
given 7 days of zosyn.  

# GVHD and Pseudomonas cellulitis: The patient had erythemic 
feet with scatter wounds ranging from .5 to 1 cm with macerated 
areas. Areas were cultured and Pseudomonas was identified. 
Infectious Disease was consulted, and the patient was treated 
with seven days of IV zosyn (4.5 mg IV q 8 hours). The patient 
was seen by wound care as well who had specific recommendations 
noted ___ the discharge worksheet.   

Recommendations: 
Soak all dressings with normal saline or commercial wound
cleanser daily. Pat dry.
Apply acetic acid 0.25% soaked 2x2 over all wound beds x 2
minutes.
Shower to remove acetic acid dressings, and or normal saline
Apply Metronidazole cream topical to open wound beds.
Place nonadherent Adaptic dressing over all wounds
Place Soft Sorb dressing posterior legs
Cover intact skin with Aquaphor ointment
Wrap BLE's with Kerlix wrap.
Secure with Medipore tape.
Change dressings daily.
After 2 weeks of Metronidazole cream, alternate with Gentamycin
cream for 2 weeks and repeat.

The patient was also seen by dermatology. They recommended 
continuing the saran wrap with ointment and wound care's 
dressing reccomendations. The patient is currently on an IL2 
trial out ___, and the IL2 was started on ___ ___ 
house and continued during his hospitalization. Upon discharge 
the patient reported significantly less pain ___ his feet and his 
feet lesions were improved.
